english.title: Contravene a CIL stop notice that has been served / displayed
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) contravened a CIL stop notice

(A)_[served on you]_
(B)_[displayed in accordance with regulation 90(6)]_

namely **(..SPECIFY CONTRAVENTION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 93(1) and (6) of the Community Infrastructure Levy Regulation 2010.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Contravention of a CIL stop notice includes causing or permitting the contravention of the notice.
(ii) An offence under this regulation may be charged by reference to a day or a longer period of time.
(iii) A person may be convicted of more than one such offence in relation to the same CIL stop notice by reference to different days or periods of time.
(iv) It is a defence for a person charged with an offence under this regulation to prove that the CIL stop notice was not served on the person; and the person did not know, and could not reasonably have been expected to know, of its existence.
(v) In determining the amount of the fine the court must have regard in particular to any financial benefit which has accrued or has appeared to accrue to the person convicted in consequence of the offence.

Either way
Summary: A fine.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limits for prosecutions
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
